newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico to increase dollar option auction.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico to increase dollar option auction.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said on Wednesday it will increase the amount of dollar put options that it will auction in August to $500 million, with the possibility of selling more if demand warrants.

The central bank said its move was aimed at lessening pressure on the exchange rate caused by what it called "important" short-term flows of cash. It also wants to increase its international reserves. The bank said in a statement it would have a second auction during the month if, during the first two weeks, 80 percent or more of the options auctioned on July 31 were exercised.
The auctions started on August 1 last year, aimed at helping the bank rebuild its international reserves.
At that time the amounts auctioned were $130 million each month, but that was later increased to $300 million a month with the possibility of a second auction.
A spokeswoman at the central bank said for the moment the increase to $500 million for the initial auction was only for August.
The central bank said that from the first of August to the present date it had exercised options for an amount of $3.26 billion.
It said important flow of funds into Mexico could persist in the next few months as Mexico's economy continues to recover and favourable conditions in international financial markets continue.
"This could lead to an increase in the tendency towards an appreciation of the exchange rate," the central bank said.
It said a continued appreciation of the currency could harm the sustainability of the economic recovery.
